pages.text:
The Aeneid
by Virgil

Author's Background
• Virgil (Publius Vergilius
Maro)
• Birth and Early Life: Born on
October 15, 70 BCE, in Andes,
near Mantua in northern Italy.
• Education: Studied in
Cremona, Milan, and Rome;
well-versed in rhetoric,
philosophy, and poetry.

Author's Background
• Literary Career: Known for
three major works:
• Eclogues (pastoral
poems)
• Georgics (poem on
farming)
• The Aeneid (epic poem)
• Patronage: Supported by
influential patrons such as
Maecenas and Augustus.
• Death: Died in 19 BCE in
Brundisium (modern Brindisi).

Context of the Literary Piece
•Historical Context
•Commissioned by Augustus: The
epic was written during the Pax
Romana, a period of relative peace
initiated by Emperor Augustus.
•Roman Propaganda: Aimed to
legitimize Augustus's rule and glorify
Rome's origins.
•Cultural Renaissance: Part of a
broader cultural revival, blending
Roman and Greek traditions.

Literary Context
•Epic Tradition: Inspired by Homer’s
epics, "The Iliad" and "The Odyssey".
•Themes: Fate, duty, piety, and the
founding of Rome.
•Structure: 	Divided 	into 	twelve
books, 	following 	the 	journey 	of
Aeneas.

Plot Story
•Main Plot
•Prologue: Aeneas's mission
to find a new homeland.
•Troy's Fall: Aeneas escapes
the burning city of Troy.

•Journey: 	Encounters various
challenges, 	including 	the
wrath of Juno and the love
affair 	with 	Dido, 	Queen 	of
Carthage.
•Underworld: 	Visits 	the
Underworld, where he learns
about his destiny and future
Roman heroes.

•War in Italy: Engages in battles to
secure a place for his people in
Latium.
•Conclusion: Aeneas defeats
Turnus, ensuring the foundation of
Rome.

Key Characters
•Aeneas: 	Trojan 	hero, 	son 	of
Anchises and Venus. Aeneas is the
protagonist of Virgil's epic poem,
The 	Aeneid. 	He 	is 	the 	son 	of
Anchises and Venus, the goddess
of beauty and erotic love.

Key Characters
•Dido: 	Queen 	of 	Carthage,
Aeneas’s lover. Dido is the queen
of 	Carthage 	and 	the 	lover 	of
Aeneas in Virgil's epic poem, The
Aeneid. 	She 	is 	a 	strong,
determined, 	and 	independent
woman 	who 	falls 	in 	love 	with
Aeneas after he claims that his
wife, Creusa, has died.

Key Characters
•Turnus: 	King of the Rutulians,
Aeneas’s primary antagonist. is
actions 	drive 	the 	conflict
between 	the 	Trojans 	and 	the
Latins, 	and 	his 	death 	at 	the
hands of Aeneas marks the end
of the war and the beginning of
a new era for the Trojans in Italy

Key Characters
•Juno: 	Goddess opposing Aeneas.
Juno is the queen of the Roman
gods and the wife of Jupiter (the
equivalent of the Greek god Zeus).
In Virgil's epic poem The Aeneid,
Juno 	is 	depicted 	as 	the 	divine
antagonist 	of 	the 	Trojan 	hero
Aeneas.

Key Characters
•Venus: 	Aeneas's 	divine
mother, aiding his journey.
Venus 	is 	the 	goddess 	of
love, beauty, and fertility in
Roman 	mythology. 	She 	is
the mother of Aeneas, the
Trojan hero who is destined
to found the city of Rome.

Significance of Work
•Cultural and Historical Impact
•Roman Identity: Reinforces Roman
values and the divine origins of
Rome.
•Augustan Propaganda: Celebrates
Augustus’s lineage and the Julian
family.
•Literary Masterpiece: Considered a
cornerstone of Western literature.

Influence on Later Works
•Medieval and Renaissance Literature:
Inspired Dante's "Divine Comedy" and
numerous other works.
•Modern Adaptations: Continues to
influence contemporary literature and
art.

Tied Up with What is Happening Today
Relevance to Modern Times
• Migration and Refugee Crises:
Echoes current global issues of
displacement and the search for a
new home.
• Leadership and Governance:
Reflections on duty, leadership, and
the founding of nations resonate with
political discourse today.
• Cultural Heritage and Identity:
Questions of national identity and
heritage are as pertinent now as in
Virgil’s time.

Themes in Contemporary Context
•Struggle and Perseverance: Aeneas’s
journey mirrors contemporary struggles for
survival and purpose.
•Globalization: The blending of cultures in
Aeneas’s story parallels modern global
interactions.
•Heroism and Sacrifice: Continues to inspire
narratives of personal and collective
sacrifice for a greater good.

The Aeneid
by Virgil

Author's Background
• Virgil (Publius Vergilius
Maro)
• Birth and Early Life: Born on
October 15, 70 BCE, in Andes,
near Mantua in northern Italy.
• Education: Studied in
Cremona, Milan, and Rome;
well-versed in rhetoric,
philosophy, and poetry.

Author's Background
• Literary Career: Known for
three major works:
• Eclogues (pastoral
poems)
• Georgics (poem on
farming)
• The Aeneid (epic poem)
• Patronage: Supported by
influential patrons such as
Maecenas and Augustus.
• Death: Died in 19 BCE in
Brundisium (modern Brindisi).

Context of the Literary Piece
•Historical Context
•Commissioned by Augustus: The
epic was written during the Pax
Romana, a period of relative peace
initiated by Emperor Augustus.
•Roman Propaganda: Aimed to
legitimize Augustus's rule and glorify
Rome's origins.
•Cultural Renaissance: Part of a
broader cultural revival, blending
Roman and Greek traditions.

Literary Context
•Epic Tradition: Inspired by Homer’s
epics, "The Iliad" and "The Odyssey".
•Themes: Fate, duty, piety, and the
founding of Rome.
•Structure: 	Divided 	into 	twelve
books, 	following 	the 	journey 	of
Aeneas.

Plot Story
•Main Plot
•Prologue: Aeneas's mission
to find a new homeland.
•Troy's Fall: Aeneas escapes
the burning city of Troy.

•Journey: 	Encounters various
challenges, 	including 	the
wrath of Juno and the love
affair 	with 	Dido, 	Queen 	of
Carthage.
•Underworld: 	Visits 	the
Underworld, where he learns
about his destiny and future
Roman heroes.

•War in Italy: Engages in battles to
secure a place for his people in
Latium.
•Conclusion: Aeneas defeats
Turnus, ensuring the foundation of
Rome.

Key Characters
•Aeneas: 	Trojan 	hero, 	son 	of
Anchises and Venus. Aeneas is the
protagonist of Virgil's epic poem,
The 	Aeneid. 	He 	is 	the 	son 	of
Anchises and Venus, the goddess
of beauty and erotic love.

Key Characters
•Dido: 	Queen 	of 	Carthage,
Aeneas’s lover. Dido is the queen
of 	Carthage 	and 	the 	lover 	of
Aeneas in Virgil's epic poem, The
Aeneid. 	She 	is 	a 	strong,
determined, 	and 	independent
woman 	who 	falls 	in 	love 	with
Aeneas after he claims that his
wife, Creusa, has died.

Key Characters
•Turnus: 	King of the Rutulians,
Aeneas’s primary antagonist. is
actions 	drive 	the 	conflict
between 	the 	Trojans 	and 	the
Latins, 	and 	his 	death 	at 	the
hands of Aeneas marks the end
of the war and the beginning of
a new era for the Trojans in Italy

Key Characters
•Juno: 	Goddess opposing Aeneas.
Juno is the queen of the Roman
gods and the wife of Jupiter (the
equivalent of the Greek god Zeus).
In Virgil's epic poem The Aeneid,
Juno 	is 	depicted 	as 	the 	divine
antagonist 	of 	the 	Trojan 	hero
Aeneas.

Key Characters
•Venus: 	Aeneas's 	divine
mother, aiding his journey.

love, beauty, and fertility in
Roman 	mythology. 	She 	is
the mother of Aeneas, the
Trojan hero who is destined
